question: The concept of Directive Principles in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of which country? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: USA
UK
Canada
Ireland
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ireland

Explanation:
The concept of Directive Principles (Part IV) in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. These principles serve as guidelines for the state in policy-making but are not enforceable by any court. Their aim is to establish social and economic democracy. The Irish Constitution also contains similar directive principles, which were adopted by the framers of the Indian Constitution. This concept is based on the ideology of a welfare state, where the government is directed to formulate policies to improve the standard of living of citizens.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ In which part of the Indian Constitution are the Directive Principles located? → Part IV

☛ From which country is the inspiration for the Directive Principles taken? → Ireland

☛ Are the Directive Principles enforceable in a court of law? → No

☛ What is the objective of the Directive Principles in the Indian Constitution? → To establish social and economic justice

☛ What is the main basis of the Directive Principles? → Welfare state
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में निदेशक सिद्धांतों की अवधारणा किस देश के संविधान से ली गई है? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है आयरलैंड

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में निदेशक सिद्धांत (भाग IV) की अवधारणा आयरलैंड के संविधान से ली गई है। ये सिद्धांत राज्य के नीति-निर्देशन के लिए मार्गदर्शक हैं, लेकिन न्यायालय में लागू करने योग्य नहीं हैं। इनका उद्देश्य सामाजिक और आर्थिक लोकतंत्र स्थापित करना है। आयरलैंड के संविधान में भी ऐसे ही निदेशक सिद्धांत हैं, जिन्हें भारतीय संविधान निर्माताओं ने अपनाया। यह अवधारणा कल्याणकारी राज्य की विचारधारा पर आधारित है, जिसमें सरकार को नागरिकों के जीवन स्तर में सुधार लाने के लिए नीतियाँ बनाने का निर्देश दिया जाता है।

question: An area with a population of over 1 million is classified as a _______. (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: mega city
district town
suburban area
metropolitan city
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is metropolitan city

Explanation:
According to the Census of India 2011, an urban area with a population of more than 1 million (10 lakh) is classified as a metropolitan city. These are large urban agglomerations that may include one or more districts. Currently, India has 53 metropolitan cities. The term 'mega city' is used for cities with a population over 10 million (1 crore). A 'district town' is the administrative headquarters of a district, while a 'suburban area' refers to the outer part of a city.

☛ Number of metropolitan cities as per Census 2011 → 53
☛ Population threshold for a mega city → over 10 million (1 crore)
☛ Delhi is classified as which type → metropolitan city
☛ Who determines metropolitan cities in India → Census of India

question: Which Supreme Court case established the 'Collegium system' for judicial appointments in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills vs. Union of India
SR Bommai vs. Union of India
The Second Judges Case (1993)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Second Judges Case (1993)

Explanation:
The Second Judges Case (1993) established the Collegium system for judicial appointments in India. Under this system, the Chief Justice of India and a group of four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court make recommendations for appointments and transfers of judges. This case overturned the earlier decision that gave primacy to the executive in the appointment process. The Collegium system ensured the independence of the judiciary by giving primacy to the judiciary itself in appointments. Later, the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) Act, 2014 was passed by Parliament to replace the Collegium system, but in 2015, the Supreme Court declared it unconstitutional, thereby restoring the Collegium system.

☛ Third Judges Case (1998) → Expanded the Collegium to a 5-member body.
☛ NJAC Act (2014) → Passed by Parliament, but struck down by the Supreme Court.
☛ Basis of Collegium system → Independence of the judiciary.
☛ Supreme Court ruling (2015) → Declared NJAC unconstitutional.
question_hi:
सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के किस मामले ने भारत में न्यायिक नियुक्तियों के लिए 'कॉलेजियम प्रणाली' की स्थापना की?
(RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: केशवानंद भारती बनाम केरल राज्य
मिनर्वा मिल्स बनाम भारत संघ

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है दूसरा न्यायाधीश मामला (1993)

Explanation:
दूसरा न्यायाधीश मामला (1993) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कॉलेजियम प्रणाली की स्थापना की। इस प्रणाली के तहत, न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति और स्थानांतरण मुख्य न्यायाधीश और चार वरिष्ठतम न्यायाधीशों के एक समूह (कॉलेजियम) द्वारा किया जाता है। इस मामले ने कार्यपालिका को नियुक्ति प्रक्रिया में प्रमुख भूमिका देने वाली पहले के फैसले को पलट दिया। कॉलेजियम प्रणाली ने न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए नियुक्ति प्रक्रिया में न्यायपालिका की प्रधानता स्थापित की। बाद में, राष्ट्रीय न्यायिक नियुक्ति आयोग (NJAC) अधिनियम, 2014 को संसद ने पारित किया, लेकिन इसे 2015 में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने असंवैधानिक घोषित कर दिया, जिससे कॉलेजियम प्रणाली बहाल हो गई।

question: Which part of the Indian Constitution, added by the 42nd Amendment, deals with tribunals? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Part IXB
Part X-A
Part XVI
Part XIV-A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part XIV-A

Explanation:
Part XIV-A of the Indian Constitution was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. This part deals with Tribunals and contains two articles: Article 323A (Administrative Tribunals) and Article 323B (Tribunals for other matters). Article 323A empowers Parliament to establish Administrative Tribunals for the adjudication of disputes related to the recruitment and service conditions of central and state government employees. Article 323B allows state governments to establish tribunals for matters such as taxation, land reforms, industrial disputes, etc. This part was introduced to ensure speedy justice in government-related cases.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which amendment added Part XIV-A? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ How many articles are in Part XIV-A? → 2 (Articles 323A and 323B)
☛ Which article deals with Administrative Tribunals? → Article 323A
☛ What does Article 323B deal with? → Tribunals for other matters
☛ Who was the Prime Minister during the 42nd Amendment? → Indira Gandhi
question_hi: 42वें संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा भाग न्यायाधिकरणों से संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: भाग IXB
भाग X-A
भाग XVI
भाग XIV-A
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग XIV-A

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का भाग XIV-A 1976 के 42वें संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। यह भाग न्यायाधिकरणों (Tribunals) से संबंधित है और इसमें दो अनुच्छेद हैं: अनुच्छेद 323A (प्रशासनिक न्यायाधिकरण) और अनुच्छेद 323B (अन्य विषयों के लिए न्यायाधिकरण)। अनुच्छेद 323A संसद को केंद्र और राज्यों के कर्मचारियों के विवादों के निपटारे के लिए प्रशासनिक न्यायाधिकरण स्थापित करने का अधिकार देता है। अनुच्छेद 323B राज्य सरकारों को कर, भूमि, औद्योगिक विवाद आदि के लिए न्यायाधिकरण स्थापित करने की अनुमति देता है। यह भाग सरकारी मामलों में त्वरित न्याय सुनिश्चित करने के लिए बनाया गया था।

question: The Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Tribes Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024, passed by the Parliament, aimed to include how many communities in the list of STs of the UT of Jammu and Kashmir? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 6
3
2
4
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 4

Explanation:
The Constitution (Jammu and Kashmir) Scheduled Tribes Order (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was passed by the Parliament. This bill aims to include 4 communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. These communities are Gaddi, Bakarwal, Sippi, and Pahari. Previously, these communities did not have Scheduled Tribe status. With the passage of this bill, these communities will benefit from reservations in government jobs, education, and other welfare schemes. This is a significant step towards the social and economic upliftment of the tribal communities in Jammu and Kashmir.

question: Which of the following committees is responsible for examining the conduct of Members of Parliament? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Committee on Public Undertakings
The Committee on Rules
The Committee on Privileges
The Public Accounts Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Committee on Privileges

Explanation:
The responsibility of examining the conduct of Members of Parliament lies with the Committee on Privileges. This committee investigates cases of breach of privilege or contempt of the House. In the Indian Parliament, both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have their own committees on privileges. It considers complaints related to the conduct of members and recommends appropriate action. Other committees like the Public Accounts Committee examine financial matters, while the Committee on Rules deals with parliamentary procedure rules.

☛ Function of Public Accounts Committee → Audit of government accounts
☛ Function of Committee on Rules → Determining parliamentary rules

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी समिति संसद सदस्यों के आचरण की जांच करने के लिए ज़िम्मेदार है? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)

नियम समिति
विशेषाधिकार समिति
सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है विशेषाधिकार समिति

Explanation:
संसद सदस्यों के आचरण की जांच करने का कार्य विशेषाधिकार समिति को सौंपा गया है। यह समिति सदस्यों के विशेषाधिकारों के उल्लंघन या अवमानना के मामलों की जांच करती है। भारतीय संसद में लोकसभा और राज्यसभा दोनों की अपनी-अपनी विशेषाधिकार समितियाँ होती हैं। यह समिति सदस्यों के आचरण से संबंधित शिकायतों पर विचार करती है और आवश्यक कार्रवाई की सिफारिश करती है। अन्य समितियाँ जैसे सार्वजनिक लेखा समिति वित्तीय मामलों की जांच करती है, जबकि नियम समिति संसदीय प्रक्रिया के नियमों से संबंधित है।

question: Right of parliament to regulate the citizenship by law is mentioned in which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 93
Article 89
Article 10
Article 11
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 11

Explanation:
Article 11 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law. This article grants Parliament the authority to legislate on the acquisition, termination, and other rules of citizenship. Article 10 deals with the continuance of the rights of citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution, while Article 9 provides for termination of citizenship upon voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign state. Article 11 is the final article of Part II (Citizenship) and enables Parliament to enact laws like the Citizenship Act, 1955. This article is significant as it ensures that citizenship rules are governed by parliamentary legislation rather than being solely based on constitutional provisions. It gives flexibility to the legislature to modify citizenship laws as per changing circumstances.

☛ What does Article 10 deal with? → Continuance of citizenship rights at the commencement of the Constitution
☛ What does Article 9 relate to? → Termination of citizenship on acquiring foreign citizenship
☛ How many articles are in Part II? → Articles 5 to 11
☛ When was the Citizenship Act enacted? → 1955
question_hi:
कानून द्वारा नागरिकता को विनियमित करने के लिए संसद के अधिकार का उल्लेख भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित में से किस अनुच्छेद में किया गया है?

अनुच्छेद 10

Explanation:

question: Sandhi-Vigrahika was in charge of which of the following departments during the Gupta period? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)

Royal palace department
Police department
solution:

During the Gupta period, the Sandhi-Vigrahika was the officer in charge of the Department of Peace and War. This position was a crucial part of the council of ministers and was responsible for foreign relations and treaties. question_hi: गुप्त काल के दौरान संधि-विग्रहिक किस विभाग के प्रभारी थे? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)

पुलिस विभाग

Explanation:
गुप्त काल में संधि-विग्रहिक शांति और युद्ध विभाग का प्रभारी होता था। यह पद मंत्रिपरिषद का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा था और इसका कार्य विदेशी संबंधों तथा संधियों का प्रबंधन करना था। संधि का अर्थ शांति और विग्रह का अर्थ युद्ध होता है, जो युद्ध और शांति से संबंधित नीतियों को दर्शाता है। गुप्त प्रशासन में प्रमुख मंत्रियों में प्रधान मंत्री, सेनापति और संधि-विग्रहिक शामिल थे। अन्य विभागों में न्याय विभाग के लिए न्यायाधीश और पुलिस विभाग के लिए दंडाधिकारी नियुक्त थे। यह प्रश्न गुप्त प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था की समझ पर आधारित है।

question: What does the Second Schedule of the Indian Constitution provide for? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Forms of oaths or affirmations
Powers of Municipalities
Allocation of seats in the Council of States
Provisions related to the President, Governors, and other officials
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provisions related to the President, Governors, and other officials

Explanation:
The Second Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions regarding the salaries, allowances, and pensions of high-ranking officials such as the President, Vice-President, Governors, Chief Justice of India, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), and the Speakers/Deputy Speakers of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. It specifies their remuneration and privileges during their tenure. Relevant articles include 59(3), 65(3), 75(6), 97, 125, 148, 158(3), 164(5), 186, 195, 221, 224, and 225. Note that Forms of Oaths or Affirmations are in the Third Schedule, Powers of Municipalities are in the Twelfth Schedule, and Allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) is in the Fourth Schedule.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की दूसरी अनुसूची में राष्ट्रपति, राज्यपालों, उपराष्ट्रपति, मुख्य न्यायाधीश, उच्च न्यायालयों के न्यायाधीशों, भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखापरीक्षक (CAG) तथा लोकसभा और राज्यसभा के अध्यक्ष/उपाध्यक्ष जैसे उच्च पदाधिकारियों के वेतन, भत्ते और पेंशन से संबंधित प्रावधान हैं। यह अनुसूची इन पदाधिकारियों के कार्यकाल के दौरान उनके पारिश्रमिक और विशेषाधिकारों को निर्धारित करती है। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 59(3), 65(3), 75(6), 97, 125, 148, 158(3), 164(5), 186, 195, 221, 224 और 225 इस अनुसूची से संबंधित हैं। ध्यान देने योग्य है कि शपथ या प्रतिज्ञान के रूप तीसरी अनुसूची में, नगर पालिकाओं की शक्तियाँ बारहवीं अनुसूची में, और राज्य परिषद में सीटों का आवंटन चौथी अनुसूची में प्रावधानित है।

question: Which of the following is a Gandhian Principle among the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Uniform Civil Code
Protection of environment
Equal justice and free legal aid
Organisation of village panchayats
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Organisation of village panchayats

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution are classified into three categories: Socialist, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual. Gandhian principles are based on the ideas of Mahatma Gandhi. Article 40 deals with the organisation of village panchayats and is a Gandhian principle. Gandhi advocated for Gram Swaraj (village self-governance), where villages would function as self-sufficient units. The Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) is a Socialist principle. Protection of the environment (Article 48A) and Equal justice and free legal aid (Article 39A) are also Socialist principles. Therefore, only the organisation of village panchayats is a Gandhian principle among the given options.

☛ Article related to village panchayats → Article 40
☛ Objective of Gandhian principles → Promote Gram Swaraj
☛ Uniform Civil Code belongs to which category → Socialist (Article 44)
☛ Environmental protection belongs to which category → Socialist (Article 48A)
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा राज्य नीति के निर्देशक सिद्धांतों (DPSP) में से एक गांधीवादी सिद्धांत है?
(RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: समान नागरिक संहिता
पर्यावरण का संरक्षण
समान न्याय और निःशुल्क विधिक सहायता

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ग्राम पंचायतों का संगठन

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांतों (DPSP) को तीन श्रेणियों में बांटा गया है: समाजवादी, गांधीवादी और उदार-बौद्धिक। गांधीवादी सिद्धांत महात्मा गांधी के विचारों पर आधारित हैं। अनुच्छेद 40 ग्राम पंचायतों के संगठन से संबंधित है और यह एक गांधीवादी सिद्धांत है। गांधीजी ग्राम स्वराज के पक्षधर थे और चाहते थे कि गाँव स्वशासी इकाइयाँ बनें। समान नागरिक संहिता (अनुच्छेद 44) समाजवादी सिद्धांत है। पर्यावरण का संरक्षण (अनुच्छेद 48A) और समान न्याय तथा निःशुल्क विधिक सहायता (अनुच्छेद 39A) भी समाजवादी सिद्धांत हैं। इस प्रकार, केवल ग्राम पंचायतों का संगठन ही गांधीवादी सिद्धांत है।

question: Which article specifies that the Governor can summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislature? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 167
Article 180
Article 174
Article 172
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 174

Explanation:
Article 174 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Governor to summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislature. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and manages the sessions of the legislature. Dissolution applies only to the Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council. The Governor can summon or prorogue either house of the legislature. Article 174 is analogous to Article 85 of the Parliament at the state level.

question: The Fundamental Duty to 'abjure violence' was initially suggested by which of the following committees/commissions? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Swaran Singh Committee
Ashok Mehta Committee
Mandal Commission
Sarkaria Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Swaran Singh Committee

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were first recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee in 1976. The committee proposed the inclusion of ten fundamental duties in the Constitution. Subsequently, through the 42nd Amendment Act (1976), the Fundamental Duties were added as Article 51A under Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution. The duty to 'abjure violence' is one of these duties, encouraging citizens to promote social harmony and national unity. Other options—Ashok Mehta Committee (Panchayati Raj), Mandal Commission (reservation), and Sarkaria Commission (Centre-State relations)—are unrelated to Fundamental Duties.

question: The rights mentioned in Part III of the Indian Constitution are termed as _____. (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Economic Rights
Legal Rights
Fundamental Rights
Foundational Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fundamental Rights

Explanation:
Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution grants Fundamental Rights to citizens. These rights are justiciable, meaning one can approach the courts if they are violated. Fundamental Rights are divided into six categories: Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (19-22), Right against Exploitation (23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29-30), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32). These rights protect democracy and individual liberty. During a National Emergency, all Fundamental Rights except Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended.

question: Under which Act was the institution of Lok Adalat given statutory status in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Constitution (42nd Amendment) Act of 1976
Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987

Explanation:
The institution of Lok Adalat was given statutory status in India under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. This Act came into force on 9 November 1995 and led to the establishment of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). Lok Adalat is an alternative dispute resolution mechanism that settles disputes through conciliation and compromise between the parties. Its decision is final and binding on all parties. Cases that can be brought to Lok Adalat include civil matters and compoundable criminal offenses. The primary objective of this system is to provide speedy and inexpensive justice to litigants, reducing the burden on regular courts. The Act also provides for the constitution of State Legal Services Authorities and District Legal Services Authorities to implement legal aid programs and organize Lok Adalats.

question: Which Amendment of the Indian Constitution introduced the concept of 'Panchayat Raj' in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: 44th Amendment
61st Amendment
74th Amendment
73rd Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 73rd Amendment

Explanation:
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX (The Panchayats) to the Constitution of India, providing constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. It introduced Articles 243 to 243O, establishing a three-tier system of rural local self-government: Gram Panchayat, Block Panchayat, and District Panchayat. The amendment mandates elections every five years and reserves seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women. It also includes the 11th Schedule with 29 subjects that can be transferred to local bodies. This amendment came into effect on 24 April 1993, marking a historic step towards decentralized democracy.

question: What is the jurisdiction of a District Judge when dealing with civil matters? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: They can only issue judgements without hearing arguments.
They can only hear appeals from lower courts.
They have original and appellate jurisdiction.
They only deal with small claims and petty disputes.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is They have original and appellate jurisdiction.

Explanation:
A District Judge in civil matters possesses original jurisdiction, meaning they can hear new cases as a court of first instance. Additionally, they have appellate jurisdiction, allowing them to hear appeals against decisions from lower courts such as Civil Judges or Munsifs. This jurisdiction is defined under the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, and other relevant laws. District Judges handle civil suits based on monetary value and exercise supervisory control over subordinate courts. Their role is crucial in the judicial hierarchy, ensuring that both original and appellate cases are adjudicated effectively.

question: Which of the following statements about Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India is INCORRECT? (RPF Constable 2024 (11/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: PILs can only be filed in the Supreme Court or High Courts in India.
PILs are the same as Writ Petitions, as both are filed for individual interests.
PIL is used to advance human rights and address issues of public concern.
PIL can be filed by any individual or organisation for the general public's benefit.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is PILs are the same as Writ Petitions, as both are filed for individual interests.

Explanation:
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) and Writ Petitions are not the same. Writ Petitions are filed for violation of individual rights (under Article 32 or 226), while PIL is meant for the benefit of the public at large. PIL addresses issues of public concern, such as human rights, environmental pollution, or corruption. PIL can be filed in the Supreme Court or High Courts, and any person or organisation can file it for the public good. The concept of PIL originated through judicial activism in the 1980s. The incorrect statement here is that PIL and writ petitions are the same, as they differ in scope and purpose. PIL relaxes the locus standi rule, allowing any public-spirited individual to approach the court.

☛ What is the principle of 'locus standi' in PIL? → Any person can file a case in public interest
☛ Which Article is NOT related to PIL? → PIL uses Article 32 and 226, but is not a separate Article
☛ What was the first landmark PIL case? → Hussainara Khatoon vs. Bihar (1979)
☛ Can PIL be filed only in the Supreme Court? → No, also in High Courts

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है PIL और रिट याचिकाएँ समान हैं, क्योंकि दोनों व्यक्तिगत हितों के लिए दायर की जाती हैं।

Explanation:
PIL (Public Interest Litigation) और रिट याचिकाएँ समान नहीं हैं। रिट याचिकाएँ व्यक्तिगत अधिकारों के उल्लंघन पर दायर की जाती हैं, जबकि PIL जनहित में दायर की जाती है। PIL का उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक चिंता के मुद्दों जैसे कि मानवाधिकार, प्रदूषण, या भ्रष्टाचार को उठाना है। PIL को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय या उच्च न्यायालय में दायर किया जा सकता है, और कोई भी व्यक्ति या संगठन इसे जनता के लाभ के लिए दायर कर सकता है। PIL का विकास न्यायिक सक्रियता के तहत हुआ, जिसमें ए.एम. अहमदी (कमेटी) के सुझावों ने भूमिका निभाई।

question: Which of the following authorities decides, how far the fundamental rights can apply to the members of the armed forces in India? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: President of India
Supreme Court
Armed forces
Parliament of India
solution:

Explanation:
Article 33 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to determine the extent to which fundamental rights apply to members of the armed forces, paramilitary forces, intelligence agencies, and police forces. This provision ensures discipline and the proper discharge of duties by restricting certain fundamental rights through legislation. The Parliament can enact laws that abrogate or restrict the fundamental rights of these forces. The President, Supreme Court, or the armed forces themselves do not have this authority. This power is exclusive to Parliament to maintain national security and operational efficiency. The purpose is to balance individual rights with the needs of the armed forces.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added Article 371A, granting special status to Nagaland? (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 12th Amendment
14th Amendment
13th Amendment
10th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 13th Amendment

Explanation:
The 13th Amendment Act, 1962 added Article 371A to the Indian Constitution, granting special status to Nagaland. This amendment restricts the application of laws passed by Parliament in matters of religious or social practices, Naga customary law and procedure, and ownership and transfer of land and resources in Nagaland. It was enacted before Nagaland became a full-fledged state on 1 December 1963. The special provisions aim to preserve the cultural and social identity of the Naga tribes. Article 371A provides that no act of Parliament applies to Nagaland in these matters unless the state's Legislative Assembly decides by a resolution to adopt it.

question: ‘The state shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment’ is a Directive Principle of State Policy inserted by the _____ of the Indian Constitution. (RPF Constable 2024 (12/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 44th Constitutional Amendment Act
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
86th Constitutional Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act

Explanation:
The phrase 'The state shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment' was inserted as Article 48-A into the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976. This Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) was added along with Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A), which includes the duty of every citizen to protect the environment. The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'Mini-Constitution' because it made extensive changes to the Constitution, including adding the words 'socialist', 'secular', and 'integrity' to the Preamble.
